title: Awake Does not keep awake !!
author: Chewbee
summary: The Awake report is too underspecified to reproduce safely today: it uses an older version, never says whether only the display sleeps or the whole PC sleeps, and does not record which Awake mode or settings were actually selected.

judgment.rationale: The issue still sounds like a plausible Awake regression, but the current public thread lacks the specific mode and behavior details needed to separate misconfiguration, expected display-off behavior, and a real keep-awake failure.
evidence: The body is on PowerToys 0.100.0 and says only choose the param plus just witness that it goes to sleep, without naming the chosen Awake mode or whether Keep screen on was enabled.
The report never states whether the whole PC enters sleep or only the display turns off.
No bug-report ZIP, screenshot, or follow-up comments are attached.
Current Awake code distinguishes between ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED only and ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED + ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED, so the missing mode detail matters directly to triage.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask the reporter to confirm the exact Awake mode and settings, what kind of sleep actually occurs, and to capture one fresh diagnostic bundle after reproducing on a current build.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys fix is plausible because the issue names Awake specifically, but the report still needs one focused clarification pass before a concrete code path can be proposed.

issue_context.summary: The report says Awake does not keep awake, but the current public evidence does not identify the selected mode or whether the actual failure is full system sleep, display-off, or another timeout-related behavior.
known_information: The report is on Microsoft Store PowerToys 0.100.0 and mentions French language settings.
The reporter says the behavior worked before and now goes to sleep.
No attachments or comments are present.
The issue is labeled Issue-Bug and Needs-Triage with no assignee.
inferences: This may be a real Awake regression, but the public report is not yet precise enough to distinguish configuration, version drift, and actual sleep-state failure.
Because Awake has separate system-awake and display-awake semantics, the missing settings detail is likely decisive.
issue_context.analysis: A targeted request for exact mode, actual observed behavior, and a fresh bug report is the cheapest path to a reliable fix hypothesis.
initial_investigation: src/modules/Awake/Awake/Core/Manager.cs computes different execution-state flags depending on whether keepDisplayOn is enabled, so the exact chosen mode directly changes expected behavior.
The absence of attachments or a later maintainer question means the dashboard should draft the first focused information request instead of pretending the issue is ready for engineering.

comment.body:
Thanks for reporting this. The missing piece is not a generic more information request; it is that Awake has different behaviors depending on the selected mode, and the current report does not say which mode was chosen or whether the whole PC slept versus only the display turning off.

**Needed**
1. Please confirm whether this still reproduces on the latest stable PowerToys build and include that version number.
2. Please reply with the exact Awake settings in use when it fails, including whether the mode is indefinite or timed and whether **Keep screen on** is enabled.
3. Please describe whether the whole PC goes to sleep or only the display turns off, and roughly how long it takes.
4. After reproducing the issue on the current build, please submit a GitHub comment containing `/bugreport` immediately afterward.

That will tell us whether this is a real keep-awake regression, a mode-specific bug, or expected display-only behavior.

proposed_fixes.title: Restore Awake's keep-awake guarantee for the exact failing mode
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The current best hypotheses are that Awake is either not applying the expected execution-state flags for the reporter's chosen mode, or the reporter is observing display-off behavior that does not actually mean the system entered sleep; the issue does not yet distinguish those cases.
plan: Collect the exact Awake mode, whether Keep screen on is enabled, and whether the whole system sleeps or only the display turns off.
Reproduce the same configuration on a current build and compare the requested mode against the actual execution-state flags and timeout behavior.
Fix the specific mode-to-execution-state mismatch or UI/settings interpretation bug if the current build still enters real sleep unexpectedly.
verification: In the exact reported Awake mode, confirm the machine stays out of real sleep for the expected duration.
If Keep screen on is disabled, confirm only the display may turn off while the system itself remains awake.

confidence.rationale: The issue names the right module but does not yet identify the selected Awake mode or even whether the reporter observed full system sleep versus expected display-off behavior.
